entries.claim: Removing exact-value credential replacement leaves common bare provider credentials unredacted because none of the remaining shape rules recognizes OpenAI-style `sk-...` tokens.
entries.failure_scenario: With `[privacy] redact_recall = true`, recall an archived turn containing `the rejected credential was sk-proj-PLANTEDSECRET` in plain prose. It is not a PEM block, URL userinfo, named header, JSON pair, assignment, flag, JWT, or GitHub token, so `redact` returns it unchanged and the credential reaches hook stdout or an MCP result. Removing provider configuration does not remove credentials already stored in transcripts.

counter_evidence.note: Rule 1 only ever replaced the exact value of the configured provider key (Redaction::of passed config.provider_api_key() at 7cf57d5:egress.rs:290-299); no rule before or after this range matches a generic sk- token in prose, so the scenario input was unredacted before unless it was that one configured key. D-06 removed rule 1 because its only source, the [provider] key, no longer exists and now refuses to load. The remaining gap is that no shape rule matches a bare sk- token, which predates this change.

entries.claim: The source scan does not fail on any socket type as claimed; it only searches for four spellings.
entries.failure_scenario: Code can add `std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::connect(...)`, `UnixListener`, or a dependency-backed type such as `socket2::Socket` under a scanned `src` directory. None contains `std::net`, `TcpStream`, `TcpListener`, or `UdpSocket`, so this test passes despite socket-capable code being present.

counter_evidence.note: tests/no_network.rs implements AC1 and D-08 as locked: a test that fails if any file under crates/*/src names std::net, TcpStream, TcpListener or UdpSocket. Unix-domain sockets are local IPC rather than a network connection, and socket2 is not a dependency of either crate.
